content:
After an extended period of developer and public beta testing, Apple is now rolling out macOS 26.6 to all users with compatible Macs. Here's what's new in this update.

macOS 26.6 now available

macOS 26.6 is now available, fixing over 150 security vulnerabilities, along with other bug fixes and performance improvements. These include a bug that incorrectly displayed some apps designed only for Intel processors as deprecated, as well as bugs affecting HDR screenshot functionality in HealthKit and Messages.

For users planning to upgrade to macOS 27 Golden Gate later this year, macOS 26.6 should have begun the indexing process to support the new Siri AI, the Siri app, and other features related to the new version of Apple Intelligence.

Apple has so far only confirmed this process for iOS 26.6 and iPadOS 26.6, but it appears the Mac will have the same arrangement. As users currently running the macOS 27 beta know, indexing can take several days, so starting it now should help reduce the wait time after upgrading later.

The official build number for macOS 26.6 is 25G72, which differs from last week's release candidate (25G70).

Have you discovered anything new in macOS 26.6? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
